chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Husayn, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you enter the mosque, praise Allah and extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). When you commence the prayer and say the Takbir, do not pass your hands beyond your ears, and do not raise your hands for supplication in the obligatory prayer to the level of passing your head."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on raising hands during prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of Samaanah and Abu Basir, establishes the specific juristic ruling (fiqh) regarding the height of hand-raising (raf' al-yadayn) during the initial Takbir and subsequent du'a in obligatory prayers. It highlights the distinct Shia practice of keeping hands at ear level for the opening Takbir and not raising them above the head for supplications within the prayer, contrasting with other schools that may raise hands higher or only at the beginning. This detail underscores the precision in ritual etiquette (adab) and the preservation of the Prophet's practice as interpreted by the Ahl al-Bayt.
